policy.purpose: Verified patristic quotation index. Every quotation must resolve to a locally vendored primary-text section and must be an exact substring of that source section after whitespace normalization.
rules: Never publish an unsourced patristic quotation.
Every quotation records Father/writer, work, section, source edition, translator, publication year, rights/provenance, topic tags and a context note.
The displayed quotation must be text from the source edition, not Mercy editorial prose.
Original-language text is included only when present in a verified reusable edition.
Context notes and doctrinal tags are editorial metadata and are visually separated from the quotation.
A quotation is not treated as a complete statement of a Father's theology; users are linked to the full local section and source volume.

quotations.work: First Letter of Clement to the Corinthians
quotations.quote: The apostles have preached the gospel to us from[176] the Lord Jesus Christ; Jesus Christ [has done so] from[177] God.
quotations.translators: Alexander Roberts, James Donaldson, F. Crombie
quotations.rights: Public domain edition; Project Gutenberg eBook 77576
quotations.context: Clement is arguing for orderly apostolic mission and the appointment of ministers in the Church amid a dispute over ecclesial order.

quotations.quote: Take ye heed, then, to have but one Eucharist.
quotations.translators: Alexander Roberts, James Donaldson, F. Crombie
quotations.rights: Public domain edition; Project Gutenberg eBook 77576
quotations.context: Ignatius exhorts the Philadelphian church to visible unity in Eucharistic worship, ministry and ecclesial life.

quotations.quote: They abstain from the Eucharist and from prayer,[1272] because they confess not the Eucharist to be the flesh of our Saviour Jesus Christ, which suffered for our sins, and which the Father, of His goodness, raised up again.
quotations.translators: Alexander Roberts, James Donaldson, F. Crombie
quotations.rights: Public domain edition; Project Gutenberg eBook 77576
quotations.context: Ignatius is opposing docetic teaching that denied the reality of Christ's flesh and suffering; his Eucharistic statement belongs inside that Christological controversy.

quotations.quote: Polycarp, and the presbyters[317] with him, to the church of God sojourning at Philippi: Mercy to you, and peace from God Almighty, and from the Lord Jesus Christ, our Saviour, be multiplied.
quotations.translators: Alexander Roberts, James Donaldson, F. Crombie
quotations.rights: Public domain edition; Project Gutenberg eBook 77576
quotations.context: The salutation identifies Polycarp together with the presbyters and addresses the Christian community at Philippi.

quotations.quote: It is not irrational, then, to form associations in opposition to existing laws, if done for the sake of the truth.
quotations.rights: Public domain edition; Project Gutenberg eBook 70561
quotations.context: Origen is answering Celsus' accusation that Christian associations were unlawful, arguing that unjust laws cannot be the final measure of truth.
